bullets.title: PLTR: +27% after Q2 earnings; 5th straight triple play, 93% YoY revenue growth
bullets.body: Palantir surged ~27% after reporting Q2 revenue of $1.94B (+93% YoY, +19% QoQ), marking the 12th consecutive quarter of YoY acceleration and fifth straight 'triple play.' Deutsche Bank upgraded to Buy with a $200 PT. The AI sovereignty narrative is gaining traction as a re-rating catalyst.

bullets.title: Photonics/Optical ban: FCC drafts rule blocking Chinese transceivers; AAOI, COHR, LITE, CIEN key beneficiaries
bullets.body: FCC is drafting rules to ban imports of new Chinese optical transceiver models used in AI data centers, a policy seen as directly benefiting U.S. suppliers. AAOI jumped ~18%, LITE jumped ~7%, COHR highlighted as most vertically integrated with a $5.81B backlog and NVDA's $2B backing. CIEN's WaveLogic 6 (only 1.6T coherent system at scale) and $7.8B backlog make it the dominant domestic alternative; VIAV seen as testing-layer beneficiary as transceiver replacements require validation.

bullets.title: AXTI: Sharp decline then 12% bounce; bull case is InP permit negotiating leverage
bullets.body: AXTI plunged (down ~55% from highs per one trader) on China InP export control fears, then bounced 12% off lows. Bulls argue AXTI's position as the key InP substrate supplier to LITE gives it negotiating leverage and that the Trump administration is aware of and working on easing InP permit constraints. Bears cite China's ability to cut off InP exports entirely. AXTI supplies InP substrates to LITE and receives upfront funding plus long-term demand visibility.

bullets.title: CRWV: +20% on Indonesia data center expansion (360MW, three facilities)
bullets.body: CoreWeave announced expansion into Indonesia with three new data centers totaling 360MW of capacity, expected online in 2028, driven by demand for localized AI compute. The stock surged ~20% on the news.

bullets.title: MU: BofA reiterates Buy/$1,550 PT; calls pullback a buying opportunity; HBM non-commodity thesis
bullets.body: BofA reiterated its Buy rating on Micron with a $1,550 PT, characterizing recent weakness as an 'enhanced buying opportunity' as memory pricing is expected to normalize in 2027–2028. Separately, Trendforce reports NVDA is evaluating multiple HBM4 variants for Rubin Ultra amid expected 2027 DRAM supply constraints, a potential tailwind for MU's HBM position.

bullets.title: NVDA: Memory LTAs seen durable; evaluating HBM4 variants for Rubin Ultra; cloud revenue share upside
bullets.body: Game theory analysis argues NVDA's memory long-term agreements (LTAs) are likely durable. NVDA is reportedly evaluating 8-Hi HBM4e, 12-Hi HBM4, and 8-Hi HBM4 alternatives for Rubin Ultra starting 3Q26 due to HBM4e validation risks and 2027 DRAM supply constraints. NVDA may also have a meaningful cloud revenue-share business. Jensen Huang launched Alpamayo 2 Super, an open frontier reasoning model for autonomous vehicles.

bullets.title: COHR, LITE, AAOI, AXTI: Photonics supply chain consolidating; Trump optical ban as secular catalyst
bullets.body: Multiple analysts frame the Trump Chinese optical transceiver ban as a multi-year secular catalyst for the entire photonics stack. COHR's 6-inch InP wafers enable 4x chip count at half cost; LITE is the sole 200Gbps EML supplier critical to NVDA GB200 and Google TPUv7; AAOI is a direct domestic beneficiary; AXTI controls InP substrate supply chain. The consensus view: whoever locks up photonics supply wins the AI infrastructure buildout.

bullets.title: SHOP: Earnings tomorrow; Strong Buy consensus, stock below analyst PT
bullets.body: Shopify reports earnings tomorrow (Aug 5). The stock carries a Strong Buy consensus rating and trades well below the average analyst price target, with strong revenue growth highlighted as the key positive thesis.

bullets.title: MRVL: Breaks $200/$217 levels; highlighted as hot semiconductor stock on AI infrastructure thesis
bullets.body: Marvell broke above $200 and subsequently $217 intraday, with multiple observers flagging it as one of the hottest semiconductor names. A detailed post on PCIe switch transition (ALAB, AVGO, MRVL) and AWS warrant dynamics was published. Marvell itself highlighted memory, bandwidth, and connectivity as critical AI infrastructure layers.

bullets.title: AMZN: Bezos files to sell $4B in stock; AWS cited as best-positioned inference cloud
bullets.body: Jeff Bezos filed to sell approximately $4.07B in Amazon stock following a recent surge, pressuring the stock ~2% in premarket. Separately, AWS is characterized as the best-positioned inference cloud provider, and AMZN is investing multiple billions in a North Carolina data center. Oracle-AWS interconnect is cited as evidence of expanding cross-cloud DCI demand.

bullets.title: MSFT: Azure hits $100B run rate; enterprise AI moving beyond single-model dependency
bullets.body: Microsoft's Azure reached a $100B annual run rate, with commentary indicating enterprise AI adoption is broadening beyond reliance on any single model, implying durable, diversified cloud AI workload growth. MSFT trading near $500 per bullish commentary.

bullets.title: ALAB, AVGO, MRVL: PCIe switch transition and AWS warrant dynamics analyzed
bullets.body: A detailed research note examined the transition from PCIe retimers to switches across Astera Labs, Broadcom, and Marvell for scale-up AI infrastructure, including AWS warrant dynamics and protocol choice implications for each vendor's competitive position.

bullets.title: TSEM: Q3 revenue guidance of $520M beats $506M consensus; Q2 EPS beats
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor guided Q3 revenue at $520M vs. $506.4M consensus, and reported Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.88 vs. $0.76 estimate — a clean beat across the board.

bullets.title: WDC: SK Hynix and SanDisk release first High Bandwidth Flash spec; AI storage convergence theme
bullets.body: SK Hynix and SanDisk (WDC) released the first OCP High Bandwidth Flash specification at FMS 2026, enabling GPUs to pull data from storage in microseconds — signaling storage is converging with memory as a tier for long-context AI inference. NVDA's FMS announcements reinforced the storage-as-memory narrative.

bullets.title: GLW: Trump admin preparing polysilicon price floor and tariffs, supportive of Hemlock/Corning
bullets.body: The Trump administration is preparing a price floor and new tariffs on polysilicon and derivative products (chips, solar panels) to protect U.S. producers, including Hemlock Semiconductor, a joint venture in which Corning (GLW) is a major partner.

bullets.title: DOCN: Shares -11% premarket on Q2 revenue miss and weak Q3 EBITDA margin guidance
bullets.body: DigitalOcean fell ~11% in premarket after Q2 revenue slightly missed expectations and the company guided Q3 EBITDA margin growth below analyst estimates, signaling near-term margin pressure.

bullets.title: META: Seen as persistently undervalued; trading at 18x fwd P/E despite consistent value creation
bullets.body: One observer notes META has historically traded at a valuation discount relative to its long-term value creation, currently at roughly 18x forward P/E, and argues the market continuously underestimates the company's earnings power.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Bespoke flags 'maybe not done' narrative; GOOG seen as better risk/reward than QQQ
bullets.body: Bespoke highlighted a potential positive inflection for Google, suggesting the GOOGL story is 'not finished.' A separate commenter argues GOOG offers better risk/reward versus QQQ and growth VC strategies. GOOGL was down ~1.5% in premarket.

bullets.title: IREN: Zuckerberg validates cautious capacity strategy; OKLO flagged alongside oil price drop
bullets.body: Mark Zuckerberg's comments on compute validated IREN's strategy of avoiding large deals and taking a cautious approach to future capacity additions following Q2 results. WTI crude fell 5.4% and Brent fell 4.7% to session lows on Hormuz reopening hopes, creating headwinds for energy-adjacent names.

bullets.title: VRT: Data center power/thermal OEMs retain multiyear backlog and pricing support
bullets.body: A cross-portfolio analysis of Sterling Infrastructure Q2 earnings flagged Vertiv and peers in electrical/thermal-management OEM as highest-conviction positive read-throughs, citing multiyear volume, backlog, and pricing support as data center infrastructure demand sustains at elevated levels.
